ai.subject: Medicine
ai.summary: Adrenal adenomas are benign, often incidental lesions, while adrenal cortical carcinoma is a rare aggressive cancer. Distinguishing them relies on imaging, hormonal work‑up, and pathology.

b: Incidence: adenoma ~5% of abdominal CTs, carcinoma <0.2 per 100,000 per year
Typical age: adenoma 40‑60 y, carcinoma 30‑50 y, slight female predominance
sections.p: Adrenal neoplasms arise from the cortex and can be benign (adenoma) or malignant (carcinoma). Both may secrete hormones, but carcinomas are more likely to cause overt endocrine syndromes and metastasise.

b: Weiss score ≥3 on pathology confirms carcinoma
Functional tumours: cortisol, aldosterone, androgens, catecholamines
sections.p: Diagnosis hinges on size, imaging characteristics, and functional status. Size >4 cm, irregular margins, high unenhanced CT attenuation (>10 HU), and rapid contrast washout suggest carcinoma.

t.b: Does the lesion have benign imaging features? Small size, low HU, rapid washout → likely adenoma; opposite → carcinoma
Is there loss of signal on out‑of‑phase images? Loss indicates intracellular lipid → adenoma
Is the tumour secreting excess hormone? Positive test guides pre‑op management and suggests functional carcinoma
When is tissue needed? Rarely, only if metastasis is suspected and surgery is not planned; risk of tumour seeding

b: Uncontrolled hypertension or hypokalaemia → suspect aldosterone‑producing tumour
Rapid weight gain, striae, glucose intolerance → cortisol excess
sections.p: Patients may present with hypertension, hypokalaemia, Cushingoid features, or incidentally on imaging. Early recognition of carcinoma is crucial because surgical resection offers the only chance of cure.

b: Weiss criteria: mitoses, atypical mitoses, necrosis, capsular invasion, etc.
TNM staging for ACC uses tumour size, nodal involvement, and distant metastasis
Adrenalectomy (open for large or invasive lesions, laparoscopic for small benign adenomas) is definitive
sections.p: Focus on distinguishing criteria, staging, and first‑line management.

b: Assuming all incidentalomas are benign without washout analysis
Skipping hormonal work‑up in a hypertensive patient
Relying on fine‑needle aspiration for definitive diagnosis
sections.p: Misinterpreting imaging or ignoring functional assessment can lead to delayed cancer diagnosis or unnecessary surgery.

whenToSeekHelp: Rapidly enlarging adrenal mass on serial imaging
New onset Cushingoid features or virilisation
